items.requirement: A requested build uses the committed repository snapshot.
The build context stays inside the repository.
A declared Dockerfile stays inside the repository and must exist.
The project explicitly selects one Dockerfile or one versioned template.
The system does not guess the project language, build command, or output directory.
Build arguments, targets, output names, and platforms are bounded and validated.
A project Dockerfile can define the image build.
An explicit versioned build template can define the image build.
A template records an immutable content digest and fixed base-image identities.
Changing a language or base-image version requires an explicit new template choice.
BuildKit performs the container build.
The built image is pushed to the local registry.
Build failures and time limits cannot pass.
The operator owns the BuildKit endpoint, registry endpoint, repository prefix, and credentials.
The project never receives registry credentials or direct BuildKit authority.
The selected platform is explicit and operator-approved.
Retries use independent attempts and preserve every attempt result.
Cancellation stops the active BuildKit request and remains a cancellation result.
The result records pass or fail and build duration.
The result records the pushed registry image and BuildKit digest.
Buster reads the pushed manifest and verifies that its bytes match the BuildKit digest.
The authoritative output is an immutable registry digest reference.
The result stores the platform and resolved build-definition identity.
Complete bounded stdout and stderr remain ordered attempt evidence.
Repository paths reject traversal and symbolic-link escape.
Build arguments cannot be used as a project-controlled secret channel.
Registry manifest reads are bounded and reject redirects and digest mismatch.
Only the narrow container.build capability can reach BuildKit and the registry.
Container build does not deploy an image or create a Kubernetes namespace.
Container build does not open a port or check application health.
Dockerfile style and policy findings remain in lint.
Build success must not depend on deployment, readiness, health, or port-forward success.
A mutable candidate tag must not be the authoritative image output.
BuildKit metadata alone must not prove that the registry stored the same digest.
The replacement cannot control the gate during implementation or parity.
The old build suite remains the sole authority until cutover.
